- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag in early days of a downward trend — true drop often occurs before model adjusts.
- After sharp price spikes, model overreacts and forecasts a prolonged upward trend — correct by reducing slope after peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in strong uptrends and too low in strong downtrends — adjust by smoothing toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) — reduce initial values by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-forecast, model often fails to adjust — apply a downward correction of 2–5% per negative sentiment unit.
